question_html: When a partner dies, does the business of the partnership firm necessarily come to an end?

options.A: Yes, death causes automatic complete legal dissolution of the firm
options.B: No, it is known as reconstitution of partnership and surviving partners continue to run the business
options.C: Yes, unless all creditors file a petition for continuation
options.D: Only if the deceased partner was the sole managing partner

answer_html: Answer: (B) Business of a partnership firm may not come to an end due to death of a partner as it is known as Reconstitution of Partnership[cite: 24].
topic_text: Introduction to Death of a Partner

question_html: According to Section 37 of the Indian Partnership Act, if continuing partners carry on business using the property of the firm without final settlement of accounts with the outgoing partner or executor, what is the option available to the outgoing partner/representative?

options.A: Only fixed bank interest at 4% p.a.
options.B: Share of profits attributable to the use of his share of property OR interest at 6% p.a. on the amount of his share
options.C: Double the capital contributed plus penalty
options.D: No share in subsequent profits under any circumstances

answer_html: Answer: (B) Under Section 37, the outgoing partner or his estate is entitled at his option to such share of profits made since he ceased to be a partner as may be attributable to the use of his share of the property or to interest at the rate of six per cent per annum[cite: 24].
topic_text: Right of Outgoing Partner to Share Subsequent Profits (Section 37)

question_html: How is the profit of the firm up to the date of death of a partner usually calculated when death occurs in the middle of an accounting year?

options.A: Through Profit and Loss Suspense Account using Time Basis or Turnover/Sales Basis
options.B: By closing all ledger accounts and preparing audited final accounts immediately on the exact day
options.C: By estimating it as exactly zero unless agreed otherwise

answer_html: Answer: (A) Such Profit is calculated through P&L Suspense account using Time Basis or Turnover or Sales Basis[cite: 24].
topic_text: Calculation of Profit up to the Date of Death

question_html: What is the primary distinction between the retirement of a partner and the death of a partner regarding accounting entries?

options.A: Revaluation is never done on death
options.B: In case of death, the executor of the deceased partner is additionally entitled to a share of profit up to the date of death
options.C: Goodwill is ignored upon death
options.D: Capital balances cannot be transferred to loan accounts on death

answer_html: Answer: (B) The basic distinction between retirement and death relates to finalisation of amount payable to the Executor of the deceased partner, who is entitled to a share of profit up to the date of death[cite: 24].
topic_text: Special Transactions in Case of Death: Payment

question_html: To which account is the balance due to a deceased partner transferred after making all necessary adjustments?

options.A: Deceased Partner's Executor's Account
options.B: Government Revenue Account
options.C: General Reserve Account

answer_html: Answer: (A) After ascertaining the amount due to the deceased partner, it should be credited to his Executor's Account[cite: 24].

question_html: What is the rate of interest payable on the amount due to the legal representative of a deceased partner from the date of death till final payment, in the absence of any agreement?

options.A: 4% per annum
options.B: 6% per annum
options.C: 10% per annum

answer_html: Answer: (B) In the absence of an agreement, the legal representative of a deceased partner is entitled to interest @ 6% p.a. on the amount due from the date of death till the date of final payment[cite: 24].
topic_text: Interest on Unsettled Dues on Death

question_html: When a Joint Life Policy amount is received on the death of a partner and the policy does not appear in the balance sheet, how is the amount treated?

options.A: Credited to Bank and credited to all partners' capital accounts in their profit sharing ratio
options.B: Credited only to the surviving partners
options.C: Credited to Revaluation Account as miscellaneous income

answer_html: Answer: (A) Bank Account is debited and Joint Life Policy Account credited, then Joint Life Policy Account is written off and credited to all old partners in Profit Sharing Ratio[cite: 24].
topic_text: Joint Life Policy Treatment on Death (Method 1)

question_html: Are legal heirs of a deceased partner entitled only to the capital account balance standing on the balance sheet?

options.A: Yes, nothing else can be claimed
options.B: No, they are entitled to capital, reserves, goodwill share, revaluation profit share, profit up to death, and JLP share[cite: 24]
options.C: Only if approved by all external creditors
options.D: Only if the partner died on the last day of the financial year

answer_html: Answer: (B) Legal representatives are entitled to capital, reserves, goodwill, revaluation profit/loss, profit up to date of death, and JLP share[cite: 24].

question_html: When separate life policies are taken on individual lives of partners and premiums are charged to P&L, what does the legal representative of a deceased partner receive upon death regarding policies?

options.A: Assured value of the deceased partner's policy plus the surrender value of policies of the remaining surviving partners in their profit-sharing ratio
options.B: Only the surrender value of his own policy
options.C: Full maturity value of all policies combined

answer_html: Answer: (A) The legal representatives would be entitled to receive assured value of deceased partner's policy and share in surrender value of other partners' life policies distributed in profit sharing ratio[cite: 24].
topic_text: Special Transactions in Case of Death: Separate Life Policy

question_html: Does the business of a partnership come to an end automatically on the death of a partner according to standard true/false rules?

options.A: True, partnership dissolves instantly
options.B: False, surviving partners continue to carry on the business[cite: 24]
options.C: True, unless court intervenes
options.D: False, but only if there are at least three remaining partners

answer_html: Answer: (B) False: Surviving partners continue to carry on the business[cite: 24].

question_html: Does a legal heir of a deceased partner automatically become a partner in the firm without agreement?

options.A: Yes, legal heirs have automatic membership rights
options.B: No, legal heirs are only entitled to the dues of the deceased partner[cite: 24]
options.C: Yes, under Indian Partnership Act section 10
options.D: Only if nominated in a bank account

answer_html: Answer: (B) False: Legal heirs of deceased partners are entitled to dues of the deceased partner[cite: 24].

question_html: Is a revaluation account opened in the books of accounts on the death of a partner?

options.A: No, revaluation is prohibited upon death
options.B: Yes, to find out the actual values of assets and liabilities[cite: 24]
options.C: Only if the firm has incurred net losses

answer_html: Answer: (B) True: To find out the actual values of the assets and liabilities, revaluation account is prepared[cite: 24].

question_html: Are reserves appearing in the balance sheet on the date of death transferred to all partners' capital accounts in their profit sharing ratio?

options.A: Yes, reserves belong to partners in the same manner as contributed capital[cite: 24]
options.B: No, they are transferred solely to the deceased partner's executor
options.C: No, they remain in the balance sheet indefinitely
options.D: Only if there are no trade payables

answer_html: Answer: (A) True: reserves belong to the partners in the same manner the capital contributed by them. Hence it is distributed to them through the capital account[cite: 24].

question_html: On the death of a partner, does the firm get the surrender value or the full sum assured of the joint life policy?

options.A: Surrender value only
options.B: Full value of sum assured of the joint life policy[cite: 24]
options.C: Half of sum assured plus surrender value

answer_html: Answer: (B) False (to statement that firm gets surrender value): On death of a partner the firm gets full value of sum assured of the joint life policy[cite: 24].
topic_text: Joint Life Policy Proceeds on Death

question_html: Are all partners (including surviving ones and the deceased partner's estate) entitled to share in the amount received from a joint life policy upon death?

options.A: Yes, all the partners are entitled to amount received from joint life policy[cite: 24]
options.B: No, only surviving partners share JLP proceeds
options.C: No, only the deceased partner's estate receives JLP proceeds
options.D: Only external insurance agents receive commission

answer_html: Answer: (A) False (to statement that only legal heirs get JLP): All the partners are entitled to amount received from joint life policy[cite: 24].

question_html: A, B and C are in partnership sharing profits and losses equally. C died on 31st October, 2021. Capital balances stood at ₹50,000, ₹75,000 and ₹1,20,000 respectively. A and B continued business without settling C's accounts. Profit made during the 3 months up to final payment on Feb 1, 2022 was ₹28,000. Under Section 37, what is C's estate entitled to if option (i) (share in subsequent profits) is chosen?
answer_html: Answer: (A) As shown in text Section 5.2, C's share = $28,000 \times \frac{1,20,000}{2,45,000} = \text{₹}13,714$[cite: 24].

question_html: In question 16, what would be the interest at 6% p.a. under option (ii) for the 3-month period?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Interest = $1,20,000 \times \frac{6}{100} \times \frac{3}{12} = \text{₹}1,800$[cite: 24].

question_html: Arun, Tarun and Neha share profits in 3:2:1. Neha dies on 31st May 2022. Sales for 2021-2022 amounted to ₹4,00,000 with a profit of ₹60,000. Sales from 1st April 2022 to 31st May 2022 were ₹1,00,000. What is Neha's share of profit up to the date of death?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Profit on sales up to date of death = $1,00,000 \times \frac{60,000}{4,00,000} = \text{₹}15,000$. Neha's share (1/6th) = $15,000 \times \frac{1}{6} = \text{₹}2,500$[cite: 24].

question_html: A, B and C share profits and losses in 2:2:1. A died on 15th April, 2022. Books are closed on 31st December. If previous year 2021 profit was ₹96,000, what is A's share of profit for 3.5 months (up to April 15)?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Profit for 3.5 months = $96,000 \times \frac{3.5}{12} = \text{₹}28,000$. A's share (2/5) = $28,000 \times \frac{2}{5} = \text{₹}11,200$[cite: 24].

question_html: In Illustration 1 (Om & Co., X, Y, Z sharing 1:2:2, Z died on 31.12.2022), average profit of preceding 3 years was calculated as ₹24,000. What is the goodwill of the firm valued at 2 years' purchase?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Goodwill = $24,000 \times 2 = \text{₹}48,000$[cite: 24].

question_html: In Illustration 1, what is Z's share of profits for the period from 1.4.2022 to 31.12.2022 (9 months) based on average profits of ₹24,000?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Z's share = $24,000 \times \frac{9}{12} \times \frac{2}{5} = \text{₹}7,200$[cite: 24].

question_html: In Illustration 2 (A, B, C sharing 1/2, 1/4, 1/4), A died on 30th September 2022. Separate life policies were taken for ₹10,000 each. Surrender value is 20% of sum assured. What is A's share of the separate life policies (A's policy + 20% of B and C's policies)?
answer_html: Answer: (A) A's policy = ₹10,000; B and C's surrender value = 20% of ₹20,000 = ₹4,000. Total = ₹14,000. A's share (1/2) = ₹7,000[cite: 24].

question_html: In Illustration 3 (ABC LLP, equal partners sharing 1/3 each, C died on 3rd Jan 2022), goodwill is valued at ₹3,000. What is the journal entry adjustment for goodwill among A, B, and C?

options.A: A's Capital Dr. ₹500, B's Capital Dr. ₹500 To C's Capital ₹1,000
options.B: C's Capital Dr. ₹1,000 To A and B ₹500 each
options.C: Goodwill A/c Dr. ₹3,000 To C's Capital ₹3,000

answer_html: Answer: (A) C's share of goodwill = ₹3,000 $\times$ (1/3) = ₹1,000, borne equally by A and B (₹500 each) in gaining ratio[cite: 24].

question_html: In Illustration 4 (B and N sharing 1/2 and 1/3 with 1/6 to reserve, making profit sharing between B and N as 3:2), N died on 1st May 2022. Average profit of 3 years is ₹42,000. What is N's share of profit for 4 months?
answer_html: Answer: (A) 4 months average profit = $42,000 \times \frac{4}{12} = \text{₹}14,000$. N's share (2/5) = $14,000 \times \frac{2}{5} = \text{₹}5,600$[cite: 24].

question_html: In Illustration 4, total 3-year profits were ₹1,26,000. What is N's share of goodwill based on 3 years' purchase of average profit?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Average profit = ₹42,000. Goodwill = $42,000 \times 3 = \text{₹}1,26,000$. N's share (2/5) = $1,26,000 \times \frac{2}{5} = \text{₹}50,400$[cite: 24].

question_html: In Illustration 5 (Diya, Riya & Kiya sharing 2:1:2, Kiya died on 30th Sep 2022), ₹2,00,000 was received against Joint Life Policy. Balance sheet JLP was ₹60,000. What net amount of JLP is distributed among partners in profit sharing ratio?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Net realization = ₹2,00,000 - ₹60,000 (Balance Sheet value) = ₹1,40,000[cite: 24].

question_html: In Illustration 5, what is Kiya's share of goodwill (firm goodwill valued at ₹1,50,000 after interest on capital)?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Kiya's share = 2/5 of ₹1,50,000 = ₹60,000[cite: 24].

question_html: A, B and C are partners sharing profits in 2:1:1. Firm has a joint life policy of ₹1,20,000 appearing in the balance sheet at surrender value of ₹20,000. On the death of A, how is the excess JLP gain of ₹1,00,000 shared among A, B and C?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Excess realization = ₹1,20,000 - ₹20,000 = ₹1,00,000. Shared in old ratio 2:1:1: A = ₹50,000, B = ₹25,000, C = ₹25,000[cite: 24].

question_html: R, J and D share profits in 7:5:4. D died on 30th June 2022. Goodwill is valued at 3 years' purchase of last 5 years' average profits. Profits are: ₹29,600; ₹28,700; ₹28,900; ₹24,000 and ₹26,800. What is D's share of goodwill?

In question 29, R, J and D share profits in 7:5:4. D died on 30th June 2022 and profits for the year 2021-2022 were ₹24,000. How much share in profit for the period 1st April 2022 to 30th June 2022 (3 months) will be credited to D's account?
answer_html: Answer: (A) 3 months profit = $24,000 \times \frac{3}{12} = \text{₹}6,000$. D's share (4/16 = 1/4) = $6,000 \times \frac{1}{4} = \text{₹}1,500$[cite: 24].

question_html: If three partners A, B & C share profits as 5:3:2, on the death of A, how much will B & C pay to A's executor on account of goodwill based on 2 years' purchase of last 3 years' average profits (profits: ₹3,29,000; ₹3,46,000; ₹4,05,000)?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Average profit = $(3,29,000+3,46,000+4,05,000)/3 = \text{₹}3,60,000$. Goodwill = $3,60,000 \times 2 = \text{₹}7,20,000$. A's share (5/10 = 1/2) = ₹3,60,000. Contributed by B and C in gaining ratio (3:2): B pays ₹2,16,000 and C pays ₹1,44,000[cite: 24].

question_html: In Practical Question 1 (Seed, Plant and Flower sharing 5:3:2, Plant died on 1st May 2022), goodwill is valued at 3 years' purchase of average profits for 4 years (profits: ₹10,000; ₹13,000; ₹12,000; ₹15,000). What is Plant's share of goodwill?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Average profit = $(10,000+13,000+12,000+15,000)/4 = \text{₹}12,500$. Goodwill = $12,500 \times 3 = \text{₹}37,500$. Plant's share (3/10) = $37,500 \times \frac{3}{10} = \text{₹}11,250$[cite: 24].

question_html: In Practical Question 1, new profit sharing ratio between Seed and Flower is 3:2. What is the gaining ratio between Seed and Flower?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Seed's gain = 3/5 - 5/10 = 1/10; Flower's gain = 2/5 - 2/10 = 2/10. Gaining ratio = 1:2[cite: 24].

question_html: In Practical Question 2 (Peter, Paul and Prince sharing 2:1:1, Peter died on 30th Sep 2022), average adjusted normal profits for goodwill valuation (after charging interest on capital) came to ₹1,07,000. What is Peter's share of goodwill (2 years' purchase)?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Total goodwill = $1,07,000 \times 2 = \text{₹}2,14,000$. Peter's share (2/4 = 1/2) = $2,14,000 \times \frac{1}{2} = \text{₹}1,07,000$[cite: 24].

question_html: In Practical Question 2, estimated annual profit for 2022 based on previous year as increased by 25% (previous year profit ₹1,50,000 less ₹6,000 undercharged insurance = ₹1,44,000 + 36,000 = ₹1,80,000 less ₹1,000 interest) is ₹1,79,000. What is Peter's share of profit up to 30th September 2022 (9 months)?
answer_html: Answer: (A) 9 months estimated profit = $1,79,000 \times \frac{9}{12} = \text{₹}1,34,250$. Peter's share (2/4) = $1,34,250 \times \frac{2}{4} = \text{₹}67,125$[cite: 24].

question_html: In Practical Question 2, total life policies include JLP of ₹1,00,000, Peter's individual policy of ₹50,000, and surrender value of Paul & Prince's policies (30% of ₹50,000 each = ₹30,000 total). Total fund = ₹1,80,000. What is Peter's share (2/4)?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Peter's share = $1,80,000 \times \frac{2}{4} = \text{₹}90,000$[cite: 24].

question_html: What is Method 2 accounting treatment for Joint Life Policy when it appears in the Balance Sheet at surrender value and a partner dies?

options.A: Bank is debited with full policy value, JLP account is credited, and excess of policy value over surrender value is credited to all partners in profit sharing ratio
options.B: JLP is ignored completely
options.C: Surrender value is debited to revaluation account
options.D: Only the deceased partner gets the full policy value without writing off JLP

answer_html: Answer: (A) Bank Account is debited with full policy value, JLP account credited, and the difference (gain) is credited to all partners' capital accounts in profit sharing ratio[cite: 24].
topic_text: Joint Life Policy Treatment on Death (Method 2)

question_html: Under Method 3 of Joint Life Policy (where JLP appears at surrender value along with JLP Reserve), how is the JLP Reserve treated upon the death of a partner?

options.A: Transferred and credited to all partners' capital accounts in their profit sharing ratio
options.B: Transferred to Bank Account
options.C: Written off against goodwill

answer_html: Answer: (A) Joint Life Policy Reserve Account is debited and credited to all partners' capital accounts in Profit Sharing Ratio[cite: 24].
topic_text: Joint Life Policy Treatment on Death (Method 3)

question_html: When calculating average net profits for goodwill valuation after charging interest on capital (as in Illustration 2), what happens if fixed capitals remain unchanged across years?

options.A: Interest on fixed capital is deducted consistently from each year's profit before finding the average
options.B: Interest on capital is added back to profits
options.C: Interest is ignored entirely
options.D: Interest is debited to revaluation account

answer_html: Answer: (A) Average net profits are computed after charging interest on fixed capital for the relevant years[cite: 24].
topic_text: Average Net Profit after Interest on Capital

question_html: In Illustration 1, a car costing ₹40,000 purchased on 1.4.2021 was wrongly written off to traveling expenses. Depreciation is 20% p.a. WDV. What is the net adjustment to profit for the year ended 31.3.2022?

options.A: Add back ₹40,000 and deduct ₹8,000 depreciation (net increase ₹32,000)
options.B: Add back ₹40,000 only without depreciation
options.C: Deduct ₹32,000

answer_html: Answer: (A) As shown in Illustration 1 solution, profit is increased by ₹40,000 and reduced by ₹8,000 depreciation, resulting in a net addition of ₹32,000[cite: 24].

question_html: In Illustration 1, X, Y, Z shared profits in 1:2:2. Z died. X and Y continue. What is the gaining ratio between X and Y?
answer_html: Answer: (A) As shown in Illustration 1 working note, X's gain = 1/3 - 1/5 = 2/15; Y's gain = 2/3 - 2/5 = 4/15. Gaining ratio = 2:4 = 1:2[cite: 24].

question_html: What is the treatment when a provision for doubtful debts found unnecessary is written back upon the death of a partner?

options.A: Provision for Doubtful Debts Account is debited and Revaluation Account (or partners' capital accounts) is credited
options.B: Provision is credited to Bank Account
options.C: Provision is debited to Executor's Account

answer_html: Answer: (A) Provision for Doubtful Debts Account is a credit balance. To close, it is debited, and Revaluation Account / Partners' Capital Accounts are credited[cite: 24].
topic_text: Provision for Doubtful Debts Unnecessary Treatment

question_html: In Illustration 2, unrecorded liability of ₹2,000 discovered on 30th Sep 2022 was recorded and immediately paid off. How does this affect partners' capital accounts?

options.A: Debited to partners' capital accounts through Revaluation (Profit & Loss Adjustment) Account in profit sharing ratio
options.B: Credited to partners' capital accounts
options.C: Ignored in capital accounts
options.D: Charged solely to the deceased partner's executor

answer_html: Answer: (A) Unrecorded liability is debited via Profit and Loss Adjustment Account to partners' capital accounts[cite: 24].

question_html: In Practical Question 1, General Reserve of ₹5,000 is distributed on the death of Plant. What amount is credited to Plant's capital account?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Plant's share of general reserve (3/10) = ₹5,000 $\times$ (3/10) = ₹1,500[cite: 24].

question_html: In Practical Question 1, fixed assets are depreciated by 10% (from ₹40,000 = ₹4,000 loss) and a worthless bill of ₹1,000 is written off. Total revaluation loss is ₹5,000. What is Plant's share of revaluation loss?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Plant's share of revaluation loss (3/10) = ₹5,000 $\times$ (3/10) = ₹1,500[cite: 24].

question_html: What is the accounting entry for transferring the balance of Profit & Loss Suspense Account at the end of the accounting period?

options.A: Transferred to Profit and Loss Account
options.B: Transferred to General Reserve Account
options.C: Transferred to Revaluation Account

answer_html: Answer: (A) At the end of the year, the Profit & Loss Suspense Account will be transferred to Profit and Loss Account[cite: 24].

question_html: When calculating profit up to the date of death on time basis, what assumption is made regarding earnings?

options.A: Profit has been earned uniformly throughout the year
options.B: Profit is earned entirely in the final month
options.C: Profit follows seasonal sales volatility

answer_html: Answer: (A) In time basis, it is assumed that profit has been earned uniformly throughout the year[cite: 24].

question_html: In turnover or sales basis for estimating profit up to death, what factors are taken into consideration?

options.A: Profit and total sales of the last year along with sales up to the date of death
options.B: Only capital balances and interest rates
options.C: Total trade payables and cash balance

answer_html: Answer: (A) We have to take into consideration the profit and the total sales of the last year and sales up to the date of death[cite: 24].

question_html: In Practical Question 1, Plant died on 1st May 2022 (4 months after 31st Dec 2021). Previous year profit was ₹15,000. Plant's share of profit based on previous year is given to him. What is Plant's share of profit (3/10th)?
answer_html: Answer: (A) 4 months previous year profit = $15,000 \times \frac{4}{12} = \text{₹}5,000$. Plant's share (3/10) = $5,000 \times \frac{3}{10} = \text{₹}1,500$[cite: 24].

question_html: In Practical Question 1, after paying ₹7,750 immediately to Plant's executors, what happens to the remaining balance due to Plant?

options.A: Remains as a loan with the firm carrying interest at 9% p.a.
options.B: Written off as bad debt
options.C: Transferred to Revaluation Account
options.D: Distributed among surviving partners as capital

answer_html: Answer: (A) The balance was to remain as a loan with the firm at 9% p.a. as interest[cite: 24].
